name: Pentagon Papers
description: The Defense Department's secret history of Vietnam decision-making, leaked by Daniel Ellsberg, showing successive administrations misled the public about the war. Alongside Watergate, the era's proof that official narratives could conceal documented deception.

name: Operation Northwoods Memoranda
description: Joint Chiefs documents proposing staged pretexts for war with Cuba — hijackings, fabricated attacks — rejected by civilian leadership. The most-cited authentic document in false-flag debates, and routinely stretched past what it proves.

name: Church Committee Reports
description: Fourteen Senate reports documenting CIA assassination plots, MKUltra, NSA watchlists, and COINTELPRO — the largest official confirmation of real intelligence-agency abuses, and the source that permanently changed the prior on 'they would never'.

name: Report from Iron Mountain
description: A hoax 'leaked government study' arguing peace would destabilize society — written as satire by Leonard Lewin, who confessed in 1972. Still circulated as authentic in militia literature; the canonical case of satire escaping its frame.

name: WikiLeaks Diplomatic Cables
description: A quarter-million leaked State Department cables revealing candid diplomacy. Their authenticity and impact made 'the documents will come out' a live expectation — energizing both legitimate transparency work and the assumption that every theory awaits its leak.
